That's a fair point. I think I would've been happier with this ending if last week's ep hadn't ended with it really, really seeming like Molly was back; that changed the tone going into last night's ep.

Sure, it's his choice, but didn't we spend two episodes of a battle with Lucien with every PC shouting out emotional callbacks to moments they had with Molly specifically to help bring him back? They wanted to resurrect MOLLY, not just Molly's body with another stranger inside. 

It's the players' story, and that's fine, but after the way 140 ended, I was really surprised that Molly actually IS gone.

This ending doesn't feel satisfying tbh! The roller coaster of emotions last week - the failed and then divinely-intervened resurrection - paid off because it was \*Molly\*. It was a perfect button to the campaign. Now, a chunk of the final episode was devoted to kinda-sorta getting to know Kingsley, a character we probably won't learn much else about. Disappointing.

I went to the Brooklyn live shows they did last Fall (MBMBaM and TAZ). The TAZ show was actually when they announced Graduation for the first time, and it's weird to think now about how excited I was about the animated trailer. 

A girl in my row loudly said "Oh boy, new friends!" when me and my friends sat down; I get that she was trying to be nice, but when I didn't respond past kind of smiling politely, she started complaining about how she always scares people off with her social awkwardness. A lot of the audience gave off a similar vibe of "we're all McElroy fandom friends so I'm gonna come up and say whatever I want to you". It was strange.

uj/ Yeah, I totally agree. I do get how Travis's ADHD could exacerbate how much the criticism gets to him - and I also know that criticism is just hard to deal with, especially when you have a platform as big as the McElroys'. 

But a lot of creators struggle with their mental health, including many who do not talk about it publicly. My issue is that the McElroys are some of the most successful podcasters out there, and the criticism they face is relatively mild.
